incidents.vector: Attackers compromised Binance systems in what the exchange described as a security breach; exact technical vector has not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: Up to $6.3 billion in funds were affected in the largest cryptocurrency heist on record; roughly $1.8 billion was frozen by Tether and Circle, but at least $1.2 billion in USDT and ETH escaped attacker control. Binance says user funds remain safe.

incidents.vector: Deployed commodity post-exploitation tools and a VBScript wiper via Group Policy against the target's network.
incidents.impact: Researchers documented the first-ever destructive, data-wiping cyberattack carried out by a Belarus-aligned state threat group, signaling deeper operational alignment between Belarusian cyber actors and Russian objectives in the war on Ukraine.

incidents.victim: Foreign ministries, defense/semiconductor/pharmaceutical firms, and telecoms across 14+ countries
incidents.vector: Used an AI agentic framework paired with a Chinese large language model and a second commercial LLM to run parallel automated intrusions, chaining identity and cloud-service flaws to gain footholds.
incidents.impact: Researchers confirmed post-exploitation activity, including a custom backdoor, at nine organizations across Latin America, Europe, Asia, and the Middle East, including foreign ministries and U.S. pharmaceutical, semiconductor, and defense firms; credential-spraying hit at least 12 more organizations.

incidents.victim: GMO (Onamae Desktop Cloud FX trading service)
incidents.vector: Hackers breached GMO's Onamae Desktop Cloud hosting service, targeting its FX foreign-exchange trading platform.
incidents.impact: Attackers demanded a $50 million ransom and leaked some stolen data on the dark web; GMO is offering a $1 million reward for information leading to the hackers.

incidents.victim: Belgian Ministry of Finance (MyMinfin tax portal)
incidents.vector: A cyberattack brought down Belgium's national tax-filing portal.
incidents.impact: The MyMinfin portal was taken offline two days before a key annual filing deadline; the Ministry of Finance extended the deadline to November 16 to compensate for the outage.

incidents.vector: Intrusion into FEC systems; the agency shut down its electronic filing system after detecting the activity.
incidents.impact: The FEC took its campaign-finance electronic filing system offline a week before the U.S. midterm elections; the agency says the outage has no impact on voting.

incidents.vector: A hacktivist group claims to have breached an Okta single sign-on service used by DHS to extract employee data.
incidents.impact: Personal and organizational data on more than 41,000 DHS employees and contractors — including ICE/CBP personnel — was published online; Okta says it has no evidence its own systems were compromised.

incidents.victim: U.S. critical infrastructure (telecom, energy, water, transportation, defense, government)
incidents.vector: A China-linked state threat group rotates through compromised home/office routers, IoT devices, and enterprise edge infrastructure (including Fortinet, Cisco, Ivanti, F5, and Palo Alto products) as rapidly rebuilt, short-lived access chains, exploiting multiple zero-days.
incidents.impact: Researchers have notified hundreds of victims, including telecom providers, government entities, defense contractors, universities, and operators in water, energy, transportation, maritime, rail, and aviation; the covert access network can be rebuilt in under two minutes, making it very difficult to fully disrupt.

incidents.victim: Japan Airlines / Japan Transocean Air (via Amadeus IT Group)
incidents.vector: Hackers accessed reservation data at Amadeus IT Group, the third-party provider that runs JAL's flight reservation, ticketing, and check-in systems.
incidents.impact: 92,000 customers had names, reservation codes, and flight information exposed; about 2,000 also had passport numbers, frequent-flyer numbers, emails, and phone numbers stolen. Flight operations and payment card data were not affected.

incidents.vector: Breach of So-net internet service provider systems.
incidents.impact: Data belonging to 2.58 million So-net customers was stolen.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached Coinbase's third-party analytics provider, Amplitude.
incidents.impact: Some Coinbase customer data was stolen through the third-party analytics breach; Coinbase says no funds were affected.

incidents.victim: University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center
incidents.vector: A ransomware attack crippled internal hospital systems.
incidents.impact: UNM diverted ambulances to other hospitals and canceled dozens of outpatient surgeries and appointments at 30+ clinics; no ransom was paid and systems were fully restored within two days. The attackers claim to have stolen patient and employee data and are offering to delete it in exchange for payment.

incidents.victim: U.S. government-affiliated organization (via Palo Alto Networks firewalls)
incidents.vector: Chained the PHP2Shell remote-code-execution flaws (CVE-2026-109618/109619) with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation bug (CVE-2026-46300) to gain root access on internet-exposed Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS management interfaces.
incidents.impact: Attackers scanned roughly 19,000 exposed firewalls, narrowed targeting to 240, and successfully breached 24 of them — compromising two servers in a U.S. government-affiliated environment with likely persistent access to internal Active Directory data, credentials, and network topology.

incidents.vector: Exploited unauthenticated vulnerabilities in a government logging service to make roughly 11 million requests extracting data from interconnected systems.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole sensitive personal data — IDs, birth and family details, health insurance, pensions, and financial and vehicle records — on roughly 750,000 citizens, about a third of the population; 82 digital services and 30+ government networks were temporarily disconnected. Officials are investigating possible foreign state involvement.

incidents.vector: Intruders used a swarm of AI agents to breach one of Warp's infrastructure suppliers.
incidents.impact: Agent trace and telemetry data was stolen for roughly 1% of Warp's customers.

incidents.vector: Hackers gained access to eSignFlow, Vanden Broele's document-signing platform.
incidents.impact: More than 120 Belgian local authorities were reportedly impacted; the company took systems offline to prevent further abuse.

incidents.victim: Florida Department of Education (Florida Student Financial Aid)
incidents.vector: An unauthorized party gained access to a system or database containing the Florida Student Financial Aid website's customer information.
incidents.impact: Names, addresses, phone numbers, genders, emails, Social Security numbers, and dates of birth were exposed for nearly 4.9 million financial-aid applicants; the site was taken offline but aid disbursements are not affected.

incidents.vector: An unidentified third party misused the company's member information retrieval API.
incidents.impact: Attackers compromised 22,519,960 customer records containing names, emails, passwords, addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, and employment information.
